contract.reader: An engineer responsible for a measurement channel who knows the GUM vocabulary of the first entry and must calibrate sensors and combine several of them
contract.problem: Producing a calibration with a defensible uncertainty, keeping it valid in the field and over time, and fusing several imperfect sensors without overstating the result
contract.outcome: Fit a calibration curve and propagate its uncertainty with covariance and the Student t factor; choose field references and calibration intervals; fuse by inverse-variance weighting, recognize correlated errors and test consistency; design and tune a complementary filter and relate it to a Kalman filter; detect and remove time offsets
contract.contribution: One reproducible path from least-squares calibration to sensor fusion, with four NumPy scripts whose real output the text interprets, and a demonstration that calibrating the gyroscope bias first cuts the fused tilt error from 0.58 to 0.14 degrees RMS
contract.evidence: Derivations on the page; four scripts (re-run 2026-10-24, output identical); JCGM 100:2008; JCGM 200:2012; ISO 28037:2026; ISO/IEC 17025:2017; ILAC-G24/OIML D 10:2022; Fraden (2016); Taylor (1997); Thrun, Burgard and Fox (2005)
contract.limitations: Illustrative data, labelled as such; straight-line and quadratic models only; one-axis tilt; Kalman filter discussed, not implemented

findings.location: Section 1.1, last paragraph, quotation '± 0.1 °C with k = 2'
findings.problem: The quotation opens with a right double quotation mark (built HTML has a closing mark before ±)
findings.whyItMatters: A visible typographic slip in the first screens of an otherwise clean page
findings.action: Write the opening mark explicitly in the source, or rephrase without quotation marks
findings.acceptance: The live page shows a left opening quotation mark, or the rephrased text

findings.location: Section 3.2, table of reference masses and indications (1280 and 360 px)
findings.problem: The seven-column table is wider than the text column even at 1280 px; the 10 kg point sits under the scroll shadow, and at 360 px four of six points are hidden
findings.whyItMatters: The reader follows a six-point fit but sees five points (two on a phone); the values are only recoverable from the script below
findings.action: Transpose the table to two columns (mass, indication) and six rows
findings.acceptance: All six data points visible without sideways scrolling at 1280 and 360 px

findings.location: Section 2 propagation law; Section 3.1 displays of b, a, S_xx and of u2(b), u2(a), u(a,b) (360 px)
findings.problem: At 360 px these displays scroll sideways without a cue; u(a,b) = -xbar s^2/S_xx is entirely off-screen although the next paragraph discusses it, and the covariance term of the propagation law is cut
findings.whyItMatters: The negative covariance is what Section 3.3 builds on (omitting it overstates the uncertainty by 27%); a phone reader does not see the formula being discussed
findings.action: Put one formula per line (gathered or aligned) and break the propagation law after the first sum
findings.acceptance: At 360 px every formula of the three displays, in particular u(a,b), is visible without sideways scrolling
